chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri reported to me from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ubaydillah al-Zurari, who reported from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Alawi al-Muhammadi, who reported from Yahya ibn Hashim al-Ghassani, who reported from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from Muadh ibn Rifa'ah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: I heard Abu Umama al-Bahili saying:

By Allah, Mu'awiya's authority will not prevent me from speaking the truth about Ali, peace be upon him. I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, say: 'Ali is the best among you, the most learned jurist among you in religion, the most knowledgeable among you of my tradition, and the best reciter among you of the Book of Allah. O Allah, I love Ali, so love him. O Allah, I love Ali, so love him.'

key_terms.أبصركم: the most insightful among you - from basar meaning clear vision
key_terms.أفضلكم: the best among you - superlative indicating supreme virtue
key_terms.أفقهكم: the most learned in jurisprudence among you

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali's superiority in knowledge and religion?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abu Umama al-Bahili, a companion of the Prophet, boldly declaring his testimony about Ali's virtues despite the political pressure of Mu'awiya's reign. The Prophet declared Ali the most excellent, the most learned in religion, the most knowledgeable of the Prophetic tradition, and the best reciter of the Quran, concluding with a supplication asking Allah to love Ali.
